credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.5 · Exercise 1
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.5: Flat ring maps
q:
Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of the ring $A$.

(1) For an $A$-module $M$ show that $S^{-1}M = S^{-1}A \otimes_A M$.

(2) Show that $S^{-1}A$ is flat over $A$.
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: localisation of modules as a tensor product and flatness of $S^{-1}A$

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.7 · Exercise 1
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.7: Localization
q: Let $A$ be a ring. Let $S \subset A$ be a multiplicative subset. Let $M$ be an $A$-module. Let $N \subset S^{-1}M$ be an $S^{-1}A$-submodule. Show that there exists an $A$-submodule $N' \subset M$ such that $N = S^{-1}N'$. (This useful result applies in particular to ideals of $S^{-1}A$.)
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: every submodule (in particular every ideal) of a localisation is extended

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.7 · Exercise 2
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.7: Localization
q:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $A$-module. Let $m \in M$.

(1) Show that $I = \{a \in A \mid am = 0\}$ is an ideal of $A$.

(2) For a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ show that the image of $m$ in $M_\mathfrak p$ is zero if and only if $I \not \subset \mathfrak p$.

(3) Show that $m$ is zero if and only if the image of $m$ is zero in $M_\mathfrak p$ for all primes $\mathfrak p$ of $A$.

(4) Show that $m$ is zero if and only if the image of $m$ is zero in $M_\mathfrak m$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $A$.

(5) Show that $M = 0$ if and only if $M_{\mathfrak m}$ is zero for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$.
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: vanishing of elements and modules is a local property (primes and maximal ideals)

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project

license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: principal localisation $A_f$ and the primes it keeps (primes not containing $f$)

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.1 · Exercise 3
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.1: Algebra
q:
Suppose that $(A, {\mathfrak m}, k)$ is a Noetherian local ring. For any finite $A$-module $M$ define $r(M)$ to be the minimum number of generators of $M$ as an $A$-module. This number equals $\dim_k M/{\mathfrak m} M = \dim_k M \otimes_A k$ by NAK.

(1) Show that $r(M \otimes_A N) = r(M)r(N)$.

(2) Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal with $r(I) > 1$. Show that $r(I^2) < r(I)^2$.

(3) Conclude that if every ideal in $A$ is a flat module, then $A$ is a PID (or a field).
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: minimal number of generators over a local ring via Nakayama, $r(M) = \dim_k M \otimes_A k$

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.3 · Exercise 1
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.3: Additive and abelian categories
q:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the category of filtered vector spaces over $k$ [Here, following Stacks Tag 0121: a filtered object is a pair $(A, F)$ of an object $A$ and a decreasing filtration $A \supset \ldots \supset F^nA \supset F^{n + 1}A \supset \ldots \supset 0$ by subobjects, $n \in \mathbf{Z}$; a morphism $(A, F) \to (B, F)$ is a morphism $\varphi : A \to B$ with $\varphi(F^iA) \subset F^iB$ for all $i$].

(1) Show that this is an additive category (explain carefully what the direct sum of two objects is).

(2) Let $f : (V, F) \to (W, F)$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{C}$. Show that $f$ has a kernel and cokernel (explain precisely what the kernel and cokernel of $f$ are).

(3) Give an example of a map of $\mathcal{C}$ such that the canonical map $\operatorname{Coim}(f) \to \operatorname{Im}(f)$ is not an isomorphism.
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: additive categories with kernels and cokernels that are not abelian ($\operatorname{Coim} \to \operatorname{Im}$ not an isomorphism)

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.3 · Exercise 2
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.3: Additive and abelian categories
q:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the category of finitely generated torsion free $R$-modules.

(1) Show that this is an additive category.

(2) Let $f : N \to M$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{C}$. Show that $f$ has a kernel and cokernel (make sure you define precisely what the kernel and cokernel of $f$ are).

(3) Give an example of a Noetherian domain $R$ and a map of $\mathcal{C}$ such that the canonical map $\operatorname{Coim}(f) \to \operatorname{Im}(f)$ is not an isomorphism.
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: kernels, cokernels and the failure of the abelian axiom in a category of modules

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.4 · Exercise 1
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.4: Tensor product
q:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\text{Mod}_R$ be the category of $R$-modules. We will say that a functor $F : \text{Mod}_R \to \text{Mod}_R$

(i) is additive if $F : \operatorname{Hom}_R(M, N) \to \operatorname{Hom}_R(F(M), F(N))$ is a homomorphism of abelian groups for any $R$-modules $M, N$,

(ii) $R$-linear if $F : \operatorname{Hom}_R(M, N) \to \operatorname{Hom}_R(F(M), F(N))$ is $R$-linear for any $R$-modules $M, N$,

(iii) right exact if for any short exact sequence $0 \to M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3 \to 0$ the sequence $F(M_1) \to F(M_2) \to F(M_3) \to 0$ is exact,

(iv) left exact if for any short exact sequence $0 \to M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3 \to 0$ the sequence $0 \to F(M_1) \to F(M_2) \to F(M_3)$ is exact,

(v) commutes with direct sums, if given a set $I$ and $R$-modules $M_i$ the maps $F(M_i) \to F(\bigoplus M_i)$ induce an isomorphism $\bigoplus F(M_i) = F(\bigoplus M_i)$.

Let $R$ be a ring. With notation as above.

(1) Give an example of a ring $R$ and an additive functor $F : \text{Mod}_R \to \text{Mod}_R$ which is not $R$-linear.

(2) Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Show that the functor $F(M) = M \otimes_R N$ is $R$-linear, right exact, and commutes with direct sums,

(3) Conversely, show that any functor $F : \text{Mod}_R \to \text{Mod}_R$ which is $R$-linear, right exact, and commutes with direct sums is of the form $F(M) = M \otimes_R N$ for some $R$-module $N$.

(4) Show that if in (3) we drop the assumption that $F$ commutes with direct sums, then the conclusion no longer holds.
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: right exactness of the tensor product and its characterisation (Eilenberg-Watts)

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.12 · Exercise 7
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.12: Depth
q:
Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Assume that $R$ is reduced, i.e., $R$ has no nonzero nilpotent elements. Assume moreover that $R$ has two distinct minimal primes $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$.

(1) Show that the sequence of $R$-modules
$$0 \to R \to R/\mathfrak p \oplus R/\mathfrak q \to R/\mathfrak p + \mathfrak q \to 0$$
is exact (check at all the spots). The maps are $x \mapsto (x \bmod \mathfrak p, x \bmod \mathfrak q)$ and $(y \bmod \mathfrak p, z \bmod \mathfrak q) \mapsto (y - z \bmod \mathfrak p + \mathfrak q)$.

(2) Show that if $\operatorname{depth}(R) \geq 2$, then $\dim(R/\mathfrak p + \mathfrak q) \geq 1$.

(3) Show that if $\operatorname{depth}(R) \geq 2$, then $U = \operatorname{Spec}(R) \setminus \{\mathfrak m\}$ is a connected topological space.

This proves a very special case of Hartshorne's connectedness theorem which says that the punctured spectrum $U$ of a local Noetherian ring of $\operatorname{depth} \geq 2$ is connected.

title: Stacks 111.28 · Exercise 2

q:
[In this section of the source, a Noetherian local ring $A$ is called Cohen-Macaulay of dimension $d$ if it has dimension $d$ and there exists a system of parameters $x_1, \ldots, x_d$ for $A$ such that $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in $A/(x_1, \ldots, x_{i-1})$ for $i = 1, \ldots, d$.]

Cohen-Macaulay rings of dimension 1. Part I: Theory.

(1) Let $(A, {\mathfrak m})$ be a local Noetherian with $\dim A = 1$. Show that if $x\in {\mathfrak m}$ is not a zerodivisor then
(a) $\dim A/xA = 0$, in other words $A/xA$ is Artinian, in other words $\{x\}$ is a system of parameters for $A$.
(b) $A$ is has no embedded prime.

(2) Conversely, let $(A, {\mathfrak m})$ be a local Noetherian ring of dimension $1$. Show that if $A$ has no embedded prime then there exists a nonzerodivisor in ${\mathfrak m}$.

credit: A. J. de Jong et al., The Stacks Project
title: Stacks 111.28 · Exercise 8
section: Chapter 111 Exercises, Section 111.28: Cohen-Macaulay rings of dimension 1
q:
[Notation from the preceding exercise of the source: $(A, \mathfrak m, k)$ is a Noetherian local ring of dimension $1$ and embedding dimension $2$, $f(n) = \dim_k {\mathfrak m}^n/{\mathfrak m}^{n + 1}$, $x, y$ are generators of $\mathfrak m$, $Gr_{\mathfrak m}(A) = k[\bar x, \bar y]/I$ for a homogeneous ideal $I$, and $F \in k[\bar x, \bar y]$ is a homogeneous element with $I \subset (F)$, with equality in all sufficiently high degrees. As in the source, a Noetherian local ring $A$ is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension $d$ if it has dimension $d$ and there exists a system of parameters $x_1, \ldots, x_d$ for $A$ such that $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in $A/(x_1, \ldots, x_{i-1})$ for $i = 1, \ldots, d$.]

Cohen-Macaulay rings of dimension 1 and embedding dimension 2. Suppose that $(A, {\mathfrak m}, k)$ is a Noetherian local ring which is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension $1$. Assume also that the embedding dimension of $A$ is $2$, i.e., assume that
$$\dim_k {\mathfrak m}/{\mathfrak m}^2 = 2.$$
Notations: $f$, $F$, $x, y\in {\mathfrak m}$, $I$ as in [the preceding exercise]. Please use any results from the problems above.

(1) Suppose that $z\in {\mathfrak m}$ is an element whose class in ${\mathfrak m}/{\mathfrak m}^2$ is a linear form $\alpha \bar x + \beta \bar y \in k[\bar x, \bar y]$ which is coprime with $F$.
(a) Show that $z$ is a nonzerodivisor on $A$.
(b) Let $d = \deg(F)$. Show that ${\mathfrak m}^n = z^{n + 1-d}{\mathfrak m}^{d-1}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. [A hint in the source is omitted.]

(2) What condition on $k$ guarantees the existence of such a $z$? (No proof required; it's too easy.)

Now we are going to assume there exists a $z$ as above. This turns out to be a harmless assumption (in the sense that you can reduce to the situation where it holds in order to obtain the results in parts (d) and (e) below).

(3) Now show that ${\mathfrak m}^\ell = z^{\ell - d + 1} {\mathfrak m}^{d-1}$ for all $\ell \geq d$.

(4) Conclude that $I = (F)$.

(5) Conclude that the function $f$ has values
$$2, 3, 4, \ldots, d-1, d, d, d, d, d, d, d, \ldots$$
license: GFDL 1.2 or later (no Invariant Sections, no Front- or Back-Cover Texts)
why: structure of one-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay local rings of embedding dimension 2 via a nonzerodivisor $z$

why: universal coefficients over a field: cohomology is dual to homology
